key_insight: The paper learns how to choose the recovery radius k adaptively so it can generate a Pareto front of feasible log-truck rescheduling plans that balance stability against operational cost.
engineering_relevance: This provides dispatchers with fast, disruption-aware recovery options for forestry logistics, helping restore feasibility while minimizing deviation from the original schedule.
method: Formulate recovery after disruptions as a sequence of neighborhood-restricted MILPs indexed by the deviation bound k.
Compute the exact minimum feasible deviation k_min to anchor the search at the most stable feasible plan.
Use REINFORCE-based reinforcement learning to adaptively select the next k from solver feedback and stop when further gains are unlikely.
evidence_signal: On weekly real-world instances from a Canadian forestry partner, the method produced richer Pareto fronts with fewer solver calls than fixed-grid and dichotomic search baselines, while staying within acceptable reoptimization times across disruption types.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the training disruptions, and the learned policy may need retraining or tuning if the operating conditions change significantly.
paper_title: Learning to recover: Adaptive local branching with reinforcement learning for log-truck routing and scheduling under disruptions
